name: Ezra
role: Priest and scribe who brought the Law back to Jerusalem
whenBasis: The seventh year of Artaxerxes (Ezra 7:7), taken as Artaxerxes I. Some date him to Artaxerxes II, ≈398 BC; see below.
summary: Priest descended from Aaron and a scribe skilled in the Law of Moses, who had set his heart to study the Law, to practise it, and to teach it in Israel. With a letter from Artaxerxes he led a company from Babylon to Jerusalem, refusing an armed escort. Finding that many, even priests, had married foreign wives, he tore his clothes and prayed; the people bound themselves to send the wives away. In Nehemiah's day he read the Law to the assembly from daybreak to noon while the Levites explained it.
body: His lineage is traced through Hilkiah, Zadok and Phinehas to Aaron. At the Ahava Canal he proclaims a fast, ashamed to ask the king for soldiers after telling him that the hand of God is on those who seek Him.

From Ezra 7:27 to 9:15 he tells the story himself. On the first day of the seventh month he stands on a wooden platform before the Water Gate and reads; the people weep, and are told not to mourn, for the day is holy. He leads one of the processions at the dedication of the wall.

moments.text: A scribe skilled in the Law
Set his heart on the Law
Weeping before the house of God
The covenant to send the wives away

later.text: The Talmud credits him with writing his book and the genealogies of Chronicles; 4 Ezra tells how he restored the scriptures after they were burned.
Taken in the text's order he came in 458 BC, thirteen years before Nehemiah; some scholars put him in 398 BC under Artaxerxes II, after Nehemiah.
traditions: 458 BC: the text's order and many commentators
398 BC: Albin van Hoonacker and some later scholars
